title: Rebuild a stock item from its events

task.text: A warehouse ledger keeps what happened, and derives how many units are on the shelf.

items: `EventStore.load(id)` returns an unmodifiable copy of the stream (empty if unknown). `append(id, expectedVersion, events)` copies the events in only if the stream has exactly `expectedVersion` events, else throws `VersionConflict`.
`StockItem.replay(history)` applies each event: `Received` adds, `Picked` subtracts, `Adjusted` adds its `delta`. `version()` is the number of events applied.

`receive`, `pick` and `adjust` check the rules, then record an event and apply it. `units` must be positive (`IllegalArgumentException`); picking more than on hand, or adjusting below zero, is an `IllegalStateException` and records nothing.
`pendingEvents()` returns what is not saved yet. `saveTo(store, id)` appends it using the version it was loaded at, then clears it.

checks.title: Any prefix of history is a past state
Commands record events and apply them
A stale save is a VersionConflict
Stored history cannot be edited from outside
The store holds events, not state

hints.text: State is never assigned directly. It is a fold over the events, and the same fold runs when you replay history and when a new command succeeds.

Write one private method that applies a single event to `onHand` and bumps `version`. `replay` calls it for each historical event. A command validates, builds the event, then calls a `record` helper that applies it and adds it to a pending list.
